home.categoryIntroAiAppsDesc: AI Apps is a build-log series that documents what it actually takes to turn an idea into a working service. It covers concrete, hands-on topics like finance automation, LLM fine-tuning, design-system integration, legacy code modernization, and PRD automation — laid out for developers and PMs with the actual prompt design, architecture decisions, and troubleshooting included, not just the finished result. If you're more curious about why a choice was made than the polished outcome, this is for you.
home.categoryIntroBizDesc: Biz covers business ideas and execution strategies built for the AI era. It works through the topics that actually matter when turning an idea into a business — business model design, market and target-customer analysis, marketing strategy, and new-venture planning — organized around real data and concrete execution steps so solo founders and planners evaluating a new venture can put it to use right away. Recommended if you have the idea but aren't sure how to turn it into a business.
home.categoryIntroJobNewsDesc: AI Job News tracks what's actually changing for knowledge workers as AI agents move from chat windows into everyday workflows. It covers the shift toward autonomous AI tools, policy and governance debates, and real adoption stories from pilot projects to production use — organized for people who want a quick read on global AI trends. Recommended if you care more about what's actually changing than the hype around it.

about.title: A solo-built <highlight>AI tech lab</highlight>
about.subtitle: NexaLab.app is a space where one person handles planning, development, and operations — building AI applications and documenting the process.
about.quote: “Building AI-powered apps and designing their architecture”
about.whatCardBody: I ship real, deployed AI app ideas (AI Apps) and turn them into sustainable businesses (Biz).
about.storyBody: I used to feel lost about how to actually put AI to work — plenty of talks and articles out there, but very few honest accounts of building a real service from idea to deployment. So I decided to pick up my own ideas and handle the planning, development, and deployment myself, recording the trial and error along the way as it happened. I believe the decisions and dead ends behind a project are often more useful than the finished result. NexaLab is where that record keeps growing.
about.coverageAiAppsDesc: The build log behind shipping an idea into a real product — prompt design, architecture decisions, and troubleshooting along the way.
about.coverageBizDesc: What AI can actually turn into a business — monetization ideas and market observations.
about.coverageToolsDesc: Ready-to-use utilities like the AI quote generator and profit calculator, free to use.
about.audienceBody: If you're figuring out how to bring AI tools into your actual work, this is for you.
about.contactBody: Feel free to reach out for collaboration, advice, or just to talk.
about.philosophyTitle: Why the tools are all free
about.philosophyBody: The quote generator, profit calculator, and SEO/GEO checker are all free. Honestly, they also bring in visitors that blog posts alone struggle to reach. That said, I didn't build them carelessly — I made these tools because I needed them myself, and the no-storage principle (nothing you enter is saved on the server) has been in place from day one. Think of it as a balance between ad revenue and visitor trust — I don't want to lose either.
about.principleBody: Blog posts start as an AI-drafted outline that I then review and edit myself. I lean on AI heavily for brainstorming, research, and first drafts, but I always try things against a real, working service before publishing. The four free tools (quote generator, profit calculator, SEO/GEO checker, report checker) get the same treatment — I use them myself and refine them from there. New posts or feature updates land roughly once or twice a week.

privacy.metaDescription: How NexaLab.app collects and handles information.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: NexaLab.app (the "Site") is a blog and free utility service planned, built, and operated individually by Kim Ho-gyun (the "Operator"). The Operator takes user privacy seriously, and this Privacy Policy explains transparently what information is collected and how it is used.
privacy.section1AutoBody: When you visit the Site, Google Analytics and Google AdSense may automatically collect information such as your IP address, cookies, browser/device information, pages visited, and time spent on the Site.
privacy.section1ToolsTitle: Information you enter into AI tools
privacy.section1ToolsBody: Text or files you enter or upload into free tools such as the AI Quote Generator, Profit Calculator, SEO/GEO Checker, llms.txt Generator, and Report Checker are used only in server memory while the request is being processed, and are discarded immediately once a response is returned. This content is never stored in any database.
privacy.section1CacheTitle: Minimal information stored as an exception
privacy.section1CacheItem1: SEO/GEO Checker: to avoid redundant re-analysis, only the checked URL and its scores are cached for up to 24 hours before expiring automatically. This information does not include personal data.
privacy.section1CacheItem2: Abuse prevention: some tools temporarily keep your IP address in server memory for up to 24 hours to prevent excessive requests; this is never written to a database.
privacy.section1AdminBody: A separate login account (email, password) used by the Site operator to manage content is handled through Supabase Auth. This is operator-only information and unrelated to regular visitors.
privacy.section2Title: 2. Purpose of Collecting and Using Information
privacy.section2Item1: Analyzing site traffic and improving service quality
privacy.section2Item2: Serving ads and personalized advertising (Google AdSense)
privacy.section2Item3: Preventing abuse and excessive requests on free tools
privacy.section3Body: In principle, personal information is not stored separately, and content entered into AI tools is discarded immediately after a response is returned. SEO/GEO Checker cache data is kept for up to 24 hours, and IP information used for abuse prevention is kept for up to 24 hours before automatic deletion. The retention period for cookies collected by Google Analytics and Google AdSense follows each service's own policy.
privacy.section4Body: The Operator does not share user information with external parties in principle. However, the following services are used to operate the Site, and each handles information under its own privacy policy.
privacy.section4Item3: Supabase (blog content and tool-result cache storage)
privacy.section5Body: The Site uses cookies issued by Google Analytics and Google AdSense to analyze traffic and serve personalized ads. You can decline cookies through your browser settings, though some features may be limited as a result. Settings such as dark mode and tool history are stored only in your browser's local storage (localStorage) and are never sent to a server.
privacy.section6Body: You may inquire about the status of your personal information at any time. Please reach out using the contact information below, and we will respond promptly.
privacy.section7Body: The Site is designed around a "no-storage" principle that avoids storing personal information whenever possible, fundamentally reducing the risk of a leak. Features that require database write access use server-only keys that are never exposed to the client (browser).
privacy.section8Body: The Site does not offer services specifically targeted at children under 14 and does not knowingly collect information from children.
privacy.section9Body: For any privacy-related inquiries, please contact us using the information below.
privacy.section10Body: Any changes to this Privacy Policy will be announced on the Site.

aiApps.metaDescription: AI-powered sub-applications NexaLab plans, builds, and operates solo for real users — Harubite.
aiApps.title: From idea to <highlight>real service</highlight>
aiApps.subtitle: NexaLab doesn't stop at the blog. The AI ideas covered here get deployed and operated as real services with real users.
aiApps.harubiteDesc: Build your own language habit, one sentence a day — start now 🌱
aiApps.harubiteLongDesc: Write and log one sentence in a foreign language every day, and AI polishes your phrasing while each entry builds into your own learning history. Instead of a heavy curriculum, it starts from the smallest possible unit — one sentence today — to help you build a habit that actually sticks.
aiApps.techStackBody: Each service is planned and built solo, on top of the stack below.
aiApps.noteBody: From model selection and prompt design to deployment, operations, and troubleshooting — this is where I collect what I've learned running AI apps for real. Related posts are gathered under the AI Apps tab on the home feed.

biz.metaDescription: From AdSense monetization experiments to tackling niche markets like workflow automation, to surviving as a solo developer — NexaLab's business record, built and tested firsthand.
biz.title: Turning code into <highlight>business</highlight>
biz.subtitle: A well-built app and a well-run business are two different things. NexaLab documents the trial and error of turning tech experiments into sustainable services.
biz.idea1Desc: Attempts (and results) at turning a side project into real revenue via AdSense, subscriptions, API sales, and more
biz.idea1LongDesc: From running Google AdSense to using free utilities (like the AI quote generator and profit calculator) to draw and convert traffic — these are experiments I've actually run, results included. Not a highlight reel, but the real numbers you run into along the way: ad approval reviews, early traffic, conversion rates.
biz.idea2Desc: How to tackle small-but-clear-problem markets — like workflow automation — with AI
biz.idea2LongDesc: Picking markets that are small but have a clear problem, and solving them with AI. The focus is validating whether you can find real users without competing head-on with big platforms.
biz.idea3Desc: The decisions and priorities a developer faces when handling planning, development, and operations alone
biz.idea3LongDesc: Planning, development, deployment, and operations — down to i18n and admin tooling — all the priorities and trade-offs you have to decide on alone, without a team. I share the judgment calls behind what got built first and what got cut.
biz.provenBody: Every idea here is something I've actually built and run in production.
biz.noteBody: Posts on monetization, market validation, and operations are gathered under the Biz tab on the home feed.

Figuring out which line items to include, how many days to budget, and what rate is fair takes time away from your actual work every time you start from scratch. Missing an item makes it awkward to bill for it later, and looking up standard pricing conventions for your industry each time is a hassle.
quoteGenerator.contentIntroSolution: Paste in your client's request and the AI Quote Generator drafts a quote in seconds — line items, estimated effort, and the reasoning behind each number.

Rebuilding a spreadsheet formula every time — or figuring out your real hourly earnings — isn't easy either.

contentFaq.question: How is the GEO score calculated?
contentFaq.answer: It scores how easy your content is for AI to cite — summaries, structured data, llms.txt, and similar signals.

contentFaq.answer: It's a reference-only static analysis and may not perfectly match real browser rendering.

contentFaq.question: Does a high score guarantee AdSense approval?
contentFaq.answer: No. This score is a reference indicator based on static analysis and does not guarantee an actual review outcome. Platforms keep their review criteria private and can change them at any time.

contentFaq.question: Why does the policy pages category carry the highest weight?
contentFaq.answer: Missing policy pages are frequently cited as an actual rejection reason, so we weight this category higher than the others.

contentFaq.question: What happens if a site blocks automatic checks?
contentFaq.answer: We'll let you know automatic checking is limited, and show you a manual checklist to review yourself instead.

contentFaq.question: How long does a check take?

contentFaq.question: Is the site content I check stored anywhere?

reportChecker.contentIntroProblem: Worried you missed something before submitting your report? Checking whether you led with the conclusion, whether sentences run too long, or whether you overused conjunctions is harder to judge on your own than it seems. And right before a deadline, there's often no time left to review at all.
reportChecker.contentIntroSolution: Paste in your document and Report Checker automatically diagnoses it across structure, sentence quality, and tone, then AI suggests improved phrasing — even a full rewrite if you want one.

contentFaq.question: What does it check?
contentFaq.answer: Rule-based checks (leading with the conclusion, sentence length, conjunction overuse, double passives, paragraph length, dated phrasing) plus AI checks.

contentFaq.question: Is my document stored anywhere?
contentFaq.answer: No. Analysis happens in memory only while the request is processed, then is discarded immediately.

contentFaq.question: Is there a length limit?
contentFaq.answer: Very long documents may reduce accuracy — we recommend pasting key sections in parts.

contentFaq.question: Can I use the AI rewrite as-is?
contentFaq.answer: Treat it as a suggestion — please verify context and facts yourself before using it.

contentFaq.question: Does it work on non-Korean documents?
contentFaq.answer: This tool is optimized for Korean text; accuracy may be lower for other languages.
